changelog: THE BOARD RUNS SMOOTHER, ESPECIALLY WHEN IT IS BUSY. Four of the glowing pieces — boss counters, raiders, the Command Power plate and the danger pill — were being lit by a blur re-derived from the artwork on every single frame, forever, whether anything was happening or not. Drifting storms were the same problem at fifty times the scale: one animating element per tile, up to fifty at once. The glow is now its own shape lit from a known rectangle, which is the difference between the browser recalculating a blur every frame and simply moving one it already has. Battles with a storm rolling across them, or a boss and raiders on screen together, are where you will notice it. IMAGES ARE READY BEFORE THEY ARE ASKED FOR, so the first time a card, a relic or a commander portrait appears it is already decoded rather than popping in a frame late. THE SWAMP HAS ITS OWN NAME NOW. A once-per-run wildcard encounter, the creature that infests it, and an achievement had all been named after somebody else's story — closely enough that it was borrowing the words rather than nodding at the idea. The encounter, its hazards and its hidden way out are unchanged and just as lethal; only the names are ours now. The situation was always the good part. FIXED: two releases had shipped carrying the same Android version code, which Android treats as the same build no matter what the version name says — so an update could be announced and then refused as already installed. The number is now checked against every version that has ever used it.
